name: Pasta alla Checca

ingredients.name: fresh vegetarian mozzarella made with vegetarian coagulants

steps: Check that the dry rigatoni contains eggless and the mozzarella label confirms vegetarian coagulants. Halve the cherry tomatoes and put them with their juices in a large serving bowl. Mince the garlic very finely, tear most of the basil by hand and cut the drained mozzarella into 1–2 cm pieces.

Mix the raw tomatoes with garlic, 35 ml olive oil, 4 g salt, black pepper and the torn basil. Leave at room temperature for 15–20 minutes while the tomatoes release some juice and the basil perfumes the oil. Do not cook this sauce; its fresh character defines the dish.

Bring 2300 ml water and 8 g salt to a rolling boil. Cook the rigatoni according to the packet until just al dente. Reserve 100 ml cooking water, then drain well. Let the pasta stand for 1 minute so its heat will warm the tomatoes without boiling or melting the cheese completely.

Tip the warm rigatoni into the raw tomato bowl and toss gently for 1 minute. Add mozzarella pieces and the remaining 10 ml olive oil, then toss once more. Add 15–30 ml reserved pasta water only if the mixture seems too dry; the tomatoes should stay visibly fresh and juicy, not form a cooked red sauce.
Divide the pasta, tomato halves and mozzarella evenly among four bowls. Top with the remaining basil leaves and serve warm or at room temperature, soon after mixing.
tips: The reviewed image shows distinct raw cherry tomato halves, soft white mozzarella pieces and basil among short pasta tubes. This is a no-cook sauce, unlike spaghetti pomodoro. Drain the mozzarella well and use only a cheese confirmed vegetarian.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
